Θαμάρ.long: Tamar, mother of Perez and Zerah by Judah, son of Jacob.
Θαμάρ.as:
Θάμαρ (Tr., Θαμάρ), ἡ (Heb. תָּמָר, Ge 38:6),
Tamar: Mt 1:3.†

θέλω.long: I will, wish, desire, am willing, intend, design.
θέλω.sd: to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas G1014 (βούλομαι) properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in
θέλω.kj: desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly))
θέλω.der: apparently strengthened from the alternate form of G138 (αἱρέομαι);
θέλω.as:
θέλω (the strengthened form ἐθέλω is found in Hom., and is the more freq. in Attic; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 415 f.),
[in LXX for חפץ ,אבה; c. neg., מאן pi., etc.;]
to will, be willing, wish, desire (more freq. than βούλομαι, q.v., in vernac. and late Gk., also in MGr.; for various views as to its relation to β., v. Thayer, 286; but v. also Bl., §24, s.v.): absol., Ro 9:16, I Co 4:1912:18, Ja 4:15; τ. θεοῦ θέλοντος, Ac 18:21; c. acc. rei, Mt 20:21, Mk 14:36, Jo 15:7, Ro 7:15, 16, I Co 4:217:36, Ga 5:17; c. inf., Mt 5:40, Mk 10:43, Jo 6:21, 67, Ro 7:21, Ga 4:9; c. acc. et inf., Mk 7:24, Lk 1:62, Jo 21:22, 23, Ro 16:19, I Co 14:5, Ga 6:13; οὐ θέλω, Mt 18:30, al.; id. c. inf., Mt 2:18, Mk 6:26, Jo 5:40, I Co 16:7; seq. ἵνα, Mt 7:12, Mk 6:25, Jo 17:24; opp. to ποιέω, πράσσω, ἐνεργέω, Ro 7:15, 19, II Co 8:10, 11, Phl 2:13; seq. ἤ (ICG, in l.; Deiss., LAE, 17924), I Co 14:19; θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσυνῄ (of his own mere will, by humility, R, mg), Col 2:18; in OT quotations, for Heb. חפץ, c. acc. pers., Mt 27:43; c. acc. rei, Mt 9:1312:7, He 10:5, 8; c. inf., I Pe 3:10; for אמר, c. inf., Ac 7:28 (v. Cremer, 726 ff.).

θεός.sd: figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very
θεός.der: of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with G3588 (ὁ)) the supreme Divinity;
θεός.as:
θεός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ (Ac 19:37 only; v. M, Pr., 60, 244), late voc., θεέ (Mt 27:46; cf. De 3:24, al.),
[in LXX chiefly for אֱלֹהִים, also for אֵל and other cognate forms, יהוה, etc.;]
a god or deity, God.
1. In polytheistic sense, a god or deity: Ac 28:6, I Co 8:4, II Th 2:4, al.; pl., Ac. 14:1119:26, Ga 4:8, al.
2. Of the one true God;
(a) anarthrous: Mt 6:24, Lk 20:38, al.; esp. c. prep. (Kühner3, iii, 605), ἀπὸ θ., Jo 3:2; ἐκ, Ac 5:39, II Co 5:1, Phl 3:9; ὑπό, Ro 13:1; παρὰ θεοῦ, Jo 1:6; παρὰ θεῷ, II Th 1:6, I Pe 2:4; κατὰ θεόν, Ro 8:27, II Co 7:9, 10; also when in gen. dependent on an anarth. noun (Bl., §46, 6), Mt 27:43, Lk 3:2, Ro 1:17, I Th 2:13; as pred., Lk 20:38, Jo 1:1, and when the nature and character rather than the person of God is meant, Ac 5:29, Ga 2:6, al. (M, Th., 14);
(b) more freq., c. art.: Mt 1:23, Mk 2:7, al. mult.; c. prep., ἀπὸ τ. θ., Lk 1:26; ἐκ, Jo 8:42, al.; παρὰ τοῦ θ., Jo 8:40; π. τῷ θ., Ro 9:14; ἐν, Col 3:3; ἐπὶ τῷ θ., Lk 1:47; ἐπὶ τὸν θ., Ac 15:19; εἰς τ. θ., Ac 24:15; πρὸς τ. θ., Jo 1:2; c. gen. pers., Mt 22:32, Mk 12:26, 27, Lk 20:37, Jo 20:17, al.; ὁ θ. μου, Ro 1:8, Phl 1:3, al.; ὁ θ. καὶ πατήρ κ. τ. λ., Ro 15:6, Eph 1:3, Phl 4:20, al.; c. gen. rei, Ro 15:5, 13, 33, II Co 1:3, I Th 5:23; τὰ τ. θεοῦ, Mt 16:23, Mk 12:17, I Co 2:11; τὰ πρὸς τὸν θ., Ro 15:17, He 2:175:1; τ. θεῷ, as a superl. (LXX, Jos 3:3), Ac 7:20, II Co 10:4; Hebraistically, of judges (Ps 81(82):6), Jo 10:34(LXX), 35.

θησαυρός.long: a store-house for precious things; hence: a treasure, a store.
θησαυρός.sd: a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or figuratively)
θησαυρός.as:
θησαυρός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< τίθημι), [in LXX chiefly for אוֹצָר;]
1.a place of safe keeping;
(a)a casket: Mt 2:11;
(b)a treasury (I Mac 3:29 and freq. in cl.);
(c)a storehouse (Ne 13:12, De 28:12, al.): Mt 13:52; metaph., of the soul, Mt 12:35; τ. καρδίας, Lk 6:45.
2.a treasure: Mt 6:19-2113:44, Lk 12:33, 34, He 11:26;θ. ἐν οὐρανῷ (v. Dalman, Words, 206 ff.), Mt 19:21, Mk 10:21, Lk 18:22; of the knowledge of God through Christ, II Co 4:7; τ. σοφίας κ. γνώσεως, Col 2:3.†

θυμόομαι.g: I provoke to anger, am full of angry passion
θυμόομαι.long: I provoke to anger; pass: I am wroth or very angry.
θυμόομαι.sd: to put in a passion, i.e. enrage
θυμόομαι.as:
θυμόω, -ῶ
(θυμός), [in LXX (chiefly in pass.) for חרה, אףחרה, אָנֵף hith., etc.;] (no act. in Attic.);
pass. (and mid.),
to be wroth or very angry: Mt 2:16.†

θνῄσκω.long: I die, am dying, am dead.
θνῄσκω.der: a strengthened form of a simpler primary (which is used for it only in certain tenses);
θνῄσκω.as:
θνήσκω,
[in LXX chiefly for מות;]
to die; pf. (M, Pr., 114), to be dead: Mt 2:20, Mk 15:44, Lk 7:128:49, Jo 11:4419:33, Ac 14:1925:19; metaph., of spiritual death, I Ti 5:6 (cf. ἀπο-, συν-απο-θνήσκω).†

θρίξ.long: hair (of the head or of animals).
θρίξ.as:
θρίξ, τριχός, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׂעָר;]
hair;
(a) of the head: Mt 3:45:3610:30, Lk 7:38, 4412:721:18, Jo 11:212:3, Ac 27:34, I Pe 3:3, Re 1:14;
(b) of animals: Mk 1:6, Re 9:8.†

θάλασσα.long: (a) the sea, in contrast to the land, (b) a particular sea or lake, e.g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.
θάλασσα.as:
θάλασσα, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָם;]
the sea: Mt 23:15, Mk 11:23, Lk 21:25, Ro 9:27, He 11:12, Ja 1:6, Ju 13, Re 7:1, al.; τὸ πέλαγος τῆς θ. (v. Tr., ut infr.), Mt 18:6; ὁ οὐρανὸς κ. ἡ γῆ κ. ἡ θ., of the whole world, Ac 4:24, al. (Hg 2:7); θ. ὑαλίνη, Re 4:615:2; of the Mediterranean, Ac 10:6, 3217:14; of the Red Sea, ἐρυθρὰ θ., Ac 7:36, I Co 10:1, 2, He 11:29; of an inland lake (as Heb. יָם), θ. τ. Γαλιλαίας, Mt 4:1815:29, Mk 1:167:31; τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jo 21:1; τ. Γ. τ. T., Jo 6:1; of the same, simply ἡ θ., Mt 4:15, Mk 2:13, al.
SYN.: πέλαγος, the vast expanse of open water"; θ., "the sea as contrasted with the land" (Tr., Syn., xiii).

θάνατος.sd: (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively)
θάνατος.as:
θάνατος, -ου, ὁ (θνήσκω),
[in LXX chiefly for מָוֶת ,מוּת, sometimes דֶּבֶר;]
death;
1. of the death of the body, whether natural or violent: Jo 11:13, Phl 2:27, He 7:23, al; opp. to ζωή, Ro 8:38, Phl 1:20; of the death of Christ, Ro 5:10, Phl 3:10, He 2:9; ῥυέσθαι (σώζειν) ἐκ θ., II Co 1:10, He 5:7; περίλυπος ἕως θανάτου, Mt 26:38, Mk 14:34; μέχρι (ἄχρι) θ., Phl 2:8, Re 2:10; πληγὴ θανάτου, a deadly wound, Re 13:3; ἰδεῖν θάνατον, Lk 2:26, He 11:5; γεύεσθαι θανάτου, Mk 9:1; ἔνοχος θανάτου, Mk 14:64; θανάτῳ τελευτᾶν (Ex 21:17, מוּת יוּמָת), Mk 7:10; death personified, Ro 6:9, I Co 15:26, Re 21:4; pl., of deadly perils, II Co 11:23.
2. Of spiritual death: Jo 5:248:51, Ro 7:10, Ja 1:155:20, I Jo 3:145:16, al.; of eternal death, Ro 1:327:5, al.; ὁ θ. ὁ δεύτερος, Re 2:1121:8 (cf. Cremer, 283 ff.; DB, iii, 114 ff.; DCG, i, 791 f.).

θεραπεύω.g: I care for, attend, serve, heal
θεραπεύω.long: I care for, attend, serve, treat, especially of a physician; hence: I heal.
θεραπεύω.sd: to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease)
θεραπεύω.as:
θεραπεύω,
[in LXX for ישׁב, etc.;]
1.to do service, serve: c. acc. pers., pass., Ac 17:25.
2. As medical term, to treat (MM, Exp., xv), cure, heal: Mt 12:10, Mk 6:5, Lk 6:7, al.; c. acc. pers., Mt 4:24, Mk 1:34, al.; seq. ἀπό, Lk 5:156:187:218:2, 43; θ. νόσον (μαλακίαν), Mt 4:23, al.
SYN.: ἰάομαι (v. Field, Notes, 60; MM, Exp., l.c.).

θυσιαστήριον.sd: a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative)
θυσιαστήριον.as:
† θυσιαστήριον, -ου, τό
(< θυσιάζω, to sacrifice), [in LXX (where the word first appears) very freq., nearly always for מִזְבֵּחַ;]
an altar:
(a) generally, Ja 2:21; pl., Ro 11:3(LXX); metaph., He 13:10 (v. Westc., in l., and esp. his add. note on the history of the word, 455 ff.);
(b) of the altar of burnt-offering in the Temple, Mt 5:23, 2423:18-20, 35, Lk 11:51, I Co 9:1310:18, He 7:13, Re 11:1;
(c) of the altar of incense in the sanctuary (Ex 30:1, al.), Lk 1:11; symbolically in Heaven, Re 6:98:3, 59:1314:1816:7 (Cremer, 292).†

θρόνος.long: a (king's) throne, seat; meton: power, dominion; a potentate.
θρόνος.sd: a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate
θρόνος.as:
θρόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כִּסֵּא, Ex 11:5, al.;]
in Hom., a seat, chair. Later, a throne, chair of state, seat of authority; of kings: metaph., of God, Mt 5:34, Ac 7:49(LXX), Re 1:4, al.; by meton., for kingly power, sovereignty, Lk 1:32, 52, Ac 2:30; for an angelic hierarchy, Col 1:16; of Christ, Mt 19:28, Re 3:21, al.; of Satan, Re 2:13; τ. θηρίου, Re 16:10; of the Apostles, Mt 19:28, Lk 22:30, cf. Re 20:4; of πρεσβύτεροι, Re 4:411:16 (on θ. τῆς χάριτος, He 4:16, v. Westc., in l.; Deiss., BS, 135).

θεάομαι.long: I see, behold, contemplate, look upon, view; I see, visit.
θεάομαι.sd: to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit
θεάομαι.der: a prolonged form of a primary verb;
θεάομαι.as:
θεάομαι, -ῶμαι,
[in LXX: II Ch 22:6 (ראה), To 2:213:6, 14, Jth 15:8, II Mac 2:43:36, III Mac 5:47*;]
to behold, look upon, contemplate, view (in early writers with a sense of wondering), in NT apparently always in literal, physical sense of "careful and deliberate vision which interprets . . . its object": c. acc. rei, Mt 11:7, Lk 7:2423:55, Jo 1:14, 324:3511:45, Ac 22:9, I Jo 1:1; c. acc. pers., Mt 22:11, Ac 21:27, Ro 15:24, I Jo 4:12; c. ptcp., Mk 16:[14], Lk 5:27, Jo 1:38, Ac 1:11; seq. ὅτι, Jo 6:5, I Jo 4:14; pass., Mt 6:123:5, Mk 16:[11].†
SYN.: v.s. θεωρέω.

θύρα.sd: a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively)
θύρα.as:
θύρα, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, also for דַּל, דֶּלֶת, etc.;]
a door: κλείειν (ἀποκ-) τὴν θ., Mt 6:6, Lk 13:25; pass., Mt 25:10, Lk 11:7, Jo 20:19, 26, Ac 21:30; ἀνοίγειν, Ac 5:19; pass., Ac 16:26, 27; κρούειν, Ac 12:13; διὰ τῆς θ., Jo 10:1, 2; πρὸς τὴν θ., Mk 1:3311:4 (WH om. τήν), Ac 3:2; τὰ πρὸς τὴν θ., the space by the door, Mk 2:2; πρὸς τῇ θ., Jo 18:16; ἐπὶ τῇ θ, Ac 5:9; πρὸ τῆς θ., Ac 12:6; ἐπὶ τῶν θ., Ac 5:23; ἡ θ. τ. μνημείου, Mt 27:60, Mk 15:4616:3. Metaph., of Christ, ἡ θ. τ. προβάτων, Jo 10:7, 9; of the Kingdom of Heaven, Lk 13:24; of opportunities, θ. πίστεως, Ac 14:27; θ. μεγάλη, I Co 16:9; θ. τ. λόγου, Col 4:3; θ. ἀνεῳγμένη (ἠνεῳγ-), II Co 2:12, Re 3:84:1; of Christ, ἑστηκὼς ἐπὶ τὴν θ. καὶ κρούων, Re 3:20; of his second coming, ἐπὶ θύραις εἶναι, Mt 24:33, Mk 13:29; πρὸ θυρῶν ἑστηκέναι, Ja 5:9.†

θέλημα.long: an act of will, will; plur: wishes, desires.
θέλημα.sd: a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination
θέλημα.der: from the prolonged form of G2309 (θέλω);
θέλημα.as:
† θέλημα, -τος, τό
(< θέλω), [in LXX chiefly for חָפֶץ, also for רָצוֹן, etc.;]
will,
(a) objectively = that which is willed: Mt 18:14, Lk 12:47, Jo 5:30, I Co 7:37, I Th 5:18, II Ti 2:26, He 10:10, Re 4:11; θ. τ. θεοῦ, Ac 22:14, Ro 2:1812:2, Eph 1:9, Col 1:94:12, I Pe 4:2; τ. κυρίου, Eph 5:17; pl., of precepts, Mk 3:35, WH, mg., Ac 13:22(LXX); ἐστιν τὸ θ., c. gen. pers., seq. ἵνα, Jo 6:39, 40, I Co 16:12; c. inf., I Pe 2:15; c. acc. et inf., I Th 4:3;
(b) subjectively = τὸ θέλειν (cf. θέλησις): Lk 23:25, Jo 1:13, I Pe 3:17, II Pe 1:21; ποιεῖν, Mt 7:2112:5021:31, Mk 3:35 (pl., WH, mg., v. supr.), Jo 4:346:387:179:31, Eph 6:6, He 10:7, 9, 3613:21, I Jo 2:17; γίνεσθαι, Mt 6:1026:42, Lk 22:42, Ac 21:14; ἡ εὐδοκία (βουλὴ) τοῦ θ., Eph 1:5, 11; ἐν τῷ θ. τοῦ θεοῦ, Ro 1:10; διὰ θ. θεοῦ, Ro 15:32, I Co 1:1, II Co 1:18:5, Eph 1:1, Col 1:1, II Ti 1:1; κατὰ τὸ θ. τ. θεοῦ, Ga 1:4, I Pe 4:19, I Jo 5:14; pl., Eph 2:3 (Cremer, 728).†

θησαυρίζω.g: I store up, treasure up, save
θησαυρίζω.long: I store up, treasure up, save, lay up.
θησαυρίζω.sd: to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively)
θησαυρίζω.kj: lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up)
θησαυρίζω.as:
θησαυρίζω,
[in LXX for צפן, etc.;]
to lay up, store up: of riches, Ja 5:3; id. c. dat. pers., Lk 12:21, II Co 12:14; c. acc. rei, I Co 16:2; θησαυροὺς ἑαυτῷ, Mt 6:19, 20; pass., II Pe 3:7; metaph., ὀργὴν ἑαντῷ, Ro 2:5 (cf. Pr 1:18, Pss. Sol 9:9).†

θερίζω.der: from G2330 (θέρος) (in the sense of the crop);
θερίζω.as:
θερίζω
(< θέρος), [in LXX chiefly for קצר;]
to reap: Mt 6:26, Lk 12:24, Ja 5:4; fig., Mt 25:24, 26, Lk 19:21, 22, Jo 4:36-38, II Co 9:6, Ga 6:7, 9, Re 14:15; c. acc., τ. σαρκικά, I Co 9:11; φθοράν, ζωὴν αἰώνιον, Ga 6:8; τ. γῆν, Re 14:16.†

θλίβω.g: I make narrow, persecute, press hard
θλίβω.long: (a) I make narrow (strictly: by pressure); I press upon, (b) I persecute, press hard.
θλίβω.kj: afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble
θλίβω.der: akin to the base of G5147 (τρίβος);
θλίβω.as:
θλίβω,
[in LXX chiefly (ὁ θλίβων) for צוּר;]
to press: c. acc. pers., Mk 3:9; ὁδὸς τεθλιμμένη, a narrow (compressed) way, Mt 7:14. Metaph. (as freq. in LXX), to oppress, afflict, distress: c. acc. pers., II Th 1:6; pass. (Vg., tribulor, tribulationem patior), II Co 1:64:87:5, I Th 3:4, II Th 1:7, I Ti 5:10, He 11:37 (cf. ἀπο-, συν-θλίβω).†

θεμελιόω.long: I found, lay the foundation (lit. and met.).
θεμελιόω.sd: to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate
θεμελιόω.as:
θεμελιόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for יסד;]
to lay the foundation of, to found: c. acc., τ. γῆν, He 1:10(LXX); pass., Mt 7:25, Lk 6:48; metaph., I Pe 5:10 (R, mg., settle); pass., Eph 3:18, Col 1:23.†

θαυμάζω.long: (a) intrans: I wonder, marvel, (b) trans: I wonder at, admire.
θαυμάζω.sd: to wonder; by implication, to admire
θαυμάζω.kj: admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder
θαυμάζω.as:
θαυμάζω,
[in LXX for נשׂא, etc.;]
to marvel, wonder, wonder at: absol., Mt 8:10, 279:3315:3121:2022:2227:14, Mk 5:2015:5, Lk 1:21 (R, txt.; ICC, in l., but v. infr.), Lk 1:638:2511:1424:41, Jo 5:207:15, Ac 2:74:1313:41, Re 17:7, 8; c. acc pers., Lk 7:9; c. acc. rei, Lk 24:12 (WH, R, mg. om.), Jo 5:28, Ac 7:31; θαῦμα μέγα, Re 17:6; πρόσωπον (LXX for נָשָׂא פָּנִים, De 10:17, al.), Ju 16; seq. διά, c. acc., Mk 6:6, Jo 7:21; seq. ἐν, c. dat. obj., Lk 1:21 (? R, mg., but v. supr); seq. ἐπί, c. dat. rei, Lk 2:334:229:4320:26, Ac 3:12; περί, Lk 2:18; ὀπίσω, Re 13:3; ὅτι, Lk 11:38, Jo 3:74:27, Ga 1:6; εἰ, Mk 15:44, I Jo 3:13. Pass. (Si 38:3, Wi 8:11): seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., II Th 1:10 (cf. ἐκ-θαυμάζω).†

θάπτω.sd: to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter
θάπτω.as:
θάπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for קבר;]
to bury: c. acc., Mt 8:21, 2214:12, Lk 9:59, 60, Ac 5:6, 9, 10; pass., Lk 16:22, Ac 2:29, I Co 15:4.†

θαρσέω.long: I am of good courage, good cheer, am bold.
θαρσέω.as:
θαρσέω, -ῶ
(v.s. θαρρέω), [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, c. neg.;]
to be of good courage: imperat., θάραει, -εῖτε, Mt 9:2, 2214:27, Mk 6:5010:49, Jo 16:33, Ac 23:11.†

θυσία.long: abstr. and concr: sacrifice; a sacrifice, offering.
θυσία.sd: sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or figuratively)
θυσία.as:
θυσία, -ας, ἡ
(θύω), [in LXX chiefly for מִנְחָה, זֶבַח;]
1. actively, an offering, sacrifice (Hdt., al.).
2. Objectively, that which is offered, a sacrifice: Mt 9:1312:7(LXX), Mk 9:49 (WH, mg.), Eph 5:2, He 10:5, 26; pl. (as usually in cl.), Mk 12:33, Lk 13:1, He 9:2310:1, 8, (θ. καὶ προσφοράς); θ. ἀνάγειν, Ac 7:41; ἀναφέρειν, He 7:27; προσφέρειν, Ac 7:42, He 5:18:3 (δῶρά τε καὶ θ.) 10:11, 1211:4; δοῦναι, Lk 2:24; pass., He 9:9; διὰ τῆς θ. αὐτοῦ, He 9:26; ἐσθίειν τὰς θ. (Le 7:15 ff.), I Co 10:18. Metaph., Phl 4:18, He 13:16; θ. πνευματικαί, I Pe 2:5; θ. ζῶσα, Ro 12:1; θ. αἰνέσεως, He 13:15; θ. . . . τ. πίστεως, Phl 2:17.†

θυγάτηρ.long: a daughter; hence (Hebraistic?), of any female descendant, however far removed; even of one unrelated: my young lady.
θυγάτηρ.sd: a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant)
θυγάτηρ.as:
θυγάτηρ, -τρός, ἡ
(for use of vocat., cf. M, Pr., 71; WH, App, 158), [in LXX for בַּת (Ge 5:4, al.), exc. Jg 21:14 B, II Ch 21:17 (אִשָּׁה);]
a daughter: Mt 9:1810:35, 3714:615:22, 28, Mk 5:356:227:26, 29, Lk 2:368:42, 4912:53, Ac 2:17(LXX)7:2121:9, He 11:24. In NT, as in OT, not in cl.;
(a) as a form of friendly address (cf. Ru 2:2, 22 al.): Mt 9:22, Mk 5:34, Lk 8:48;
(b) metaph.: sc. κυρίου, II Co 6:18 (cf. Is 43:6);
(c) of posterity: θ. Ἀαρών, Lk 1:5; Ἀβραάμ, Lk 13:16 (cf. Is 16:2, IV Mac 15:28, al);
(d) of habitation: θ. Σιών, Ἱερουσαλήμ, Mt 21:5(LXX), Lk 23:28, Jo 12:15 (cf. Is 1:8, Za 9:9, al.).†

θορυβέω.g: I disturb greatly, terrify, strike with panic
θορυβέω.long: I disturb greatly, terrify, strike with panic; mid: I show agitation of mind.
θορυβέω.sd: to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor
θορυβέω.kj: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar
θορυβέω.as:
θορυβέω, -ῶ
(< θόρυβος), [in LXX: Na 2:3(4) (רעל ho.), Da LXX 8:17 (בּעת ni.), Jg 3:26, Wi 18:19, Si 40:6*;]
1.to make a noise or uproar: mid., of loud and ostentatious lamentation, Mt 9:23, Mk 5:39, Ac 20:10.
2. Trans., to trouble, throw into confusion: τ. πόλιν, Ac 17:5.†

θερισμός.long: reaping, harvest; met: the harvest, crop.
θερισμός.as:
θερισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< θερίζω), [in LXX chiefly for קָצִיר;]
harvest;
(a) the act: Jo 4:35;
(b) the time: fig., Mt 13:30, 39, Mk 4:29
(c) the crop: fig., Mt 9:37, 38, Lk 10:2, Re 14:15.†

Θωμᾶς.long: Thomas, also called Didymus, one of the Twelve.
Θωμᾶς.as:
Θωμᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Heb. תְּאוֹם, a twin; cf. δίδυμος),
Thomas the Apostle: Mt 10:3, Mk 3:18, Lk 6:15, Jo 11:1614:520:24-2821:2, Ac 1:13.†

Θαδδαῖος.long: Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles.
Θαδδαῖος.as:
Θαδδαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. תַּדִאַי, תַּדַּי),
Thaddæus: Mt 10:3, Mk 3:18 (WH, mg., Λεββαῖος, q.v.).†

θανατόω.long: I put to death, subdue; pass: I am in danger of death, am dead to, am rid of, am parted from.
θανατόω.kj: become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify
θανατόω.der: from G2288 (θάνατος) to kill (literally or figuratively)
θανατόω.as:
θανατόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for מוּת hi., ho., also for הרג, etc.;]
to put to death: c. acc., Mt 10:2126:5927:1, Mk 13:1214:55, Lk 21:16, II Co 6:9, I Pe 3:18; pass., Ro 8:36. Metaph.: Ro 8:13; pass., c. dat, (in relation to), Ro 7:4.†

θρηνέω.long: intrans: I lament, wail; trans: I bewail.
θρηνέω.as:
θρηνέω, -ῶ
(< θρῆνος), [in LXX chiefly for ילל hi., also for קין pil., etc.;]
1. intrans., to lament, wail: Mt 11:17, Lk 7:32, Jo 16:20.
2. Trans., to bewail: c. acc. pers., Lk 23:27.†
SYN.: κλαίω, κόπτομαι, λυπέομαι, πενθέω (v. Tr., Syn., § lxv).

θλῖψις.kj: afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble
θλῖψις.as:
θλίψις (LTr., θλῖψις), -εως, ἡ
(< θλίβω), [in LXX for צָרָה, etc.;]
pressure (Arist.). In LXX and NT metaph., tribulation, affliction, distress: Mt 24:9, 21, 29, Mk 13:19, 24, Jo 16:21, Ac 7:1111:19, Ro 12:12, II Co 1:4, 84:176:47:48:2, 13, Phl 4:14, II Th 1:6, Ja 1:27, Re 1:92:9, 227:14; c. ἀνάγκη (q.v.), I Th 3:7; στενοχωρία (which from the order of the words would appear to be the stronger term), Ro 2:98:35; διωγμός, Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17, II Th 1:4; θ. ἔχω, Jo 16:33, I Co 7:28, Re 2:10; ἔρχεσθαι ἐπί, Ac 7:11; ἐν θλίψει, I Th 1:6; pl., Ac 7:1014:2220:23, Ro 5:3, Eph 3:13, I Th 3:3, He 10:33; τ. Χριστοῦ, Col 1:24; θ. τῆς καρδίας, II Co 2:4; θ. ἐγείρειν, Phl 1:17.†
SYN.: ἀνάγκη, διωγμός, στενοχωρία (v. supr., and cf. Tr., Syn, § lv; Lft., Notes, 45).

θεριστής.as:
** θεριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< θερίζω), [in LXX: Da LXX Bel32, TH Bel33*;]
a reaper: Mt 13:30, 39.†

θῆλυς.as:
θῆλυς, -εια, -υ,
[in LXX chiefly for נְקֵבָה;]
female: as subst., ἡ θ., a female, a woman: Ro 1:26, 27; τὸ θ., Mt 19:4, Mk 10:6, Ga 3:28.†

θαυμάσιος.sd: wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle
θαυμάσιος.as:
θαυμάσιος, -α, -ον
(< θαῦμα), [in LXX chiefly for פּלא ni. (n. pl. = נִפְלָאוֹת);]
wonderful; n. pl., wonders: Mt 21:15.†

θηλάζω.as:
θηλάζω
(< θηλή, a breast), [in LXX chiefly for ינק hi.;]
1. of the mother, to suckle: Mt 24:19, Mk 13:17, Lk 21:23.
2. Of the young, to suck: Mt 21:16; μαστούς, Lk 11:27 (cf. Jb 3:12, Ca 8:1, al.).†

θαυμαστός.long: to be wondered at, wonderful, marvelous.
θαυμαστός.as:
θαυμαστός, -ή, -όν
(< θαυμάζω), [in LXX for פֶּלֶא and cogn. forms (Ps 117(118):22, 23118(119):129, Is 25:1, al.), יָרֵא ni. (Ex 15:11, Ps 64(65):5, al.), אַדִּיר (Ps 8:1, 992(93):4), etc.;]
wonderful, marvellous: Mt 21:42(LXX), Mk 12:11(LXX), Jo 9:30, I Pe 2:9, Re 15:1, 3.†

θύω.long: I sacrifice, generally an animal; hence: I kill.
θύω.sd: properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose)
θύω.as:
θύω,
[in LXX chiefly for זבח, also for שׁחט, etc.;]as in cl.;
1.to offer first fruits to a god.
2.to sacrifice by slaying a victim, offer sacrifice: Ac 14:13; c. dat. pers., Ac 14:18; id. c. acc. rei, I Co 10:20.
3.to slay, kill: Jo 10:10, Ac 10:1311:7; c. acc. rei, Lk 15:23, 27, 30; pass., Mt 22:4; τὸ πάσχα (Ex 12:21), Mk 14:12; pass., Lk 22:7, I Co 5:7.†

θροέομαι.long: I disturb, agitate; pass: I am troubled, alarmed.
θροέομαι.sd: to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten
θροέομαι.as:
θροέω, -ῶ
(< θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX: Ca 5:4 [המה*;]
in cl.,
1.to cry aloud, make an outcry.
2.to utter aloud.
3. In NT (and LXX), pass., to be troubled, as by an alarm: Mt 24:6, Mk 13:7, Lk 24:37 (WH, mg.), II Th 2:2 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 126).†

θέρος.as:
θέρος, -ους, τό
(θέρω, to heat), [in LXX chiefly for קַיִץ;]
summer: Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28, Lk 21:30.†

θόρυβος.long: (a) din, hubbub, confused noise, outcry, (b) riot, disturbance.
θόρυβος.as:
θόρυβος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX for הָמוֹן, etc.;]
a noise, uproar, tumult, as of an excited mob: Mt 26:527:24, Mk 14:2, Ac 20:121:3424:18; of mourners, = ὄχλος θορυβούμενος, Mk 5:38.†

θεωρέω.long: I look at, gaze, behold; I see, experience, discern; I partake of.
θεωρέω.sd: to be a spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge))
θεωρέω.kj: behold, consider, look on, perceive, see
θεωρέω.der: from a derivative of G2300 (θεάομαι) (perhaps by addition of G3708 (ὁράω));
θεωρέω.as:
θεωρέω, -ῶ
(< θεωρός, a spectator, < θεάομαι), [in LXX chiefly for ראה, חזה;] (pres. and impf. only, exc. Jo 7:3 (fut.), Mt 28:1, Lk 23:48, Jo 8:51, Re 11:12 (aor.); Bl., §24);
1. (cl.), to look at, gaze, behold: absol., Mt 27:55, Mk 15:40, Lk 23:35; seq. πῶς, Mk 12:41; ποῦ, Mk 15:47; c. acc. pers., Jo 6:40, 6212:4516:10-19, Ac 3:1620:3825:24, Re 11:11, 12; id. c. ptcp., Mk 5:15, Lk 10:18, Jo 6:1910:1220:12, 14, I Jo 3:17; c. acc. rei, Mt 28:1, Lk 14:2921:623:48, Jo 2:236:27:3, Ac 4:138:13; id. c. ptcp., Jo 20:6, Ac 7:5610:11; seq. ὅτι, Ac 19:26.
2. In popular lang. (Kennedy, Sources, 155; Bl., §24, s.v. ὁρᾶν), in pres. and impf. = ὁράω, to see, perceive, discern: seq. ὅτι, Mk 16:4, Jo 4:1912:19, Ac 19:2627:10; πόσαι, Ac 21:20; πηλίκος, He 7:4; c. acc. rei, Mk 5:38; id. c. ptcp., Ac 17:1628:6; c. acc. pers., Mk 3:11, Jo 14:19, Ac 9:717:22; πνεῦμα, Lk 24:37; τὸ π., Jo 14:17; seq. ὅτι, Jo 9:8; c. ptcp., Lk 24:39.
3. Hebraistically, to experience, partake of: τ. θάνατον, Jo 8:51 (cf. Ps 88(89):49); τ. δόξαν, Jo 17:24 (cf. ἀνα-, παρα-θερρέω).†

θηρίον.long: properly: a wild beast, hence: any animal; met: a brute.
θηρίον.der: diminutive from the same as G2339 (θήρα);
θηρίον.as:
θηρίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of θήρ), [in LXX chiefly for חַיָּה;]
a wild beast, beast: Mk 1:13, Ac 11:628:4, 5, Tit 1:12, He 12:20, Ja 3:7, Re 6:8; of Antichrist, Re 11:7, 13-20.†

θαμβέομαι.long: I amaze; pass: I am amazed (almost terrified).
θαμβέομαι.as:
θαμβέω, -ῶ
(θάμβος), [in LXX for בּעת ni., pi., etc.;]
1.to be amazed.
2. In late Gk., to astonish, terrify (II Ki 22:5): pass., Mk 1:2710:32; seq. ἐπί, c. dat. rei, Mk 10:24.†

θυγάτριον.as:
* θυγάτριον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of θυγάτηρ),
a little daughter, a term of endearment used in late Gk. (cf. B1., § 27, 4): Mk 5:237:25.†

θυρωρός.as:
θυρωρός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ
(< θύρα, + οὖρος, a guardian), [in LXX: IV Ki 7:11 (שׁוֹעֵר), Ez 44:11 (פְּקֻדָּה), II Ki 4:6, I Es 7*;]
a door-keeper, porter: ὁ, Mk 13:34, Jo 10:3; ἡ, Jo 18:16, 17.†

θερμαίνομαι.long: I warm; mid: I warm myself.
θερμαίνομαι.as:
θερμαίνω
(< θερμός), [in LXX chiefly for חמם;]
to warm, heat; mid., to warm oneself: Mk 14:54, 67, Jo 18:18, 25, Ja 2:16.†

Θεόφιλος.long: Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank, to whom the Gospel and Acts are dedicated.
Θεόφιλος.sd: friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian

θυμιάω.sd: to fumigate, i.e. offer aromatic fumes
θυμιάω.der: from a derivative of G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of smoking);
θυμιάω.as:
θυμιάω, -ῶ
(< θύω), [in LXX (with -άζω) chiefly for קטר pi., hi.;]
to burn incense: Lk 1:9.†

θυμίαμα.sd: an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself
θυμίαμα.as:
θυμίαμα, -τος, τό
(< θυμιάω), [in LXX chiefly for קְטֹרֶת;]
fragrant stuff for burning, incense: ἡ ὥρα τοῦ θ., Lk 1:10; θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θ. (Ex 30:27, al.), Lk 1:11; pl., Re 5:88:3, 418:13.†

Θάρα.sd: Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham
Θάρα.as:
Θαρά (Rec. Θάρα), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. תֶּרַח),
Terah (Ge 11): Lk 3:34.†

θραύω.long: I crush, break, shatter; met: I break down.
θραύω.as:
θραύω,
[in LXX for רצץ (De 28:33, Is 42:458:6), etc.;]
to break in pieces, shatter; metaph., to break down: Lk 4:18(LXX).†

θυμός.as:
θυμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< θύω), [in LXX most freq. for אַף, also for חֵמָה, חָרוֹן, etc., 30 words in all;]
passion, hot anger, wrath: He 11:27; ὀργὴ καὶ θ., Ro 2:8, cf. Col 3:8; πικρία κ. θ., Eph 4:31; πλησθῆναι, πλήρης θυμοῦ, Lk 4:28, Ac 19:28; θ. ἔχειν, Re 12:12; οἶνος τ. θυμοῦ τ. πορνείας (cf. Je 28 (51):7), Re 14:818:3 (cf. Re 17:2); οἶνος τ. θ. τ. θεοῦ, Re 14:10; id., τ. ὀργῆς τ. θεοῦ, Re 16:1919:15; ὁ θ. τ. θεοῦ, Re 14:1915:1, 716:1; pl., impulses or outbursts of anger: ἔρις, ζῆλος, θυμοὶ, ἐριθίαι, II Co 12:20, Ga 5:20 (Cremer, 287, 733).†
SYN.: ὀργή, παροργισμός.

θάμβος.long: astonishment, amazement (allied to terror or awe).
θάμβος.as:
θάμβος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX for פַּחַד, etc.;]
amazement: Lk 4:365:9, Ac 3:10.†

θεμέλιος.long: (properly, an adj: belonging to the foundation), a foundation stone.
θεμέλιος.sd: something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively)
θεμέλιος.as:
θεμέλιος, -ον
(< τίθημι), [in LXX for אַרְמוֹן, מוֹסָד, etc.;]
of or for a foundation; as subst., ὁ θ. (sc. λίθος), a foundation stone, foundation: Lk 6:48, 4914:29 (but v. Deiss., BS, 123); pl., οἰ θ. (cl.), He 11:10, Re 21:14, 19; neut., τὸ θ. (Arist., Phys., vi, 6, 10, LXX and later writers), Ac 16:26; metaph., Ro 15:20, I Co 3:10-12, Eph 2:20, I Ti 6:19, II Ti 2:19, He 6:1.†

θεραπεία.long: care, attention, especially medical attention (treatment); hence almost: healing; meton: those who render service.
θεραπεία.sd: attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics
θεραπεία.as:
θεραπεία, -ας, ἡ
(θεραπεύω), [in LXX for עֲבָדִים, Ge 45:16 (cf. Es 5:2), etc.;]
1.service.
2.healing: Lk 9:11 (Field, Notes, 60), Re 22:2.
3. Collective, household attendants, servants: Lk 12:42 (LXX, Ge 45:16, Es 5:2, etc.).†

θηρεύω.long: I hunt, seek to catch or entrap; met: I lay hold of.
θηρεύω.sd: to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at
θηρεύω.as:
θηρεύω
(< θήρα), [in LXX for צוּד, etc.;]
to hunt, ensnare, catch: metaph., Lk 11:54.†

θεῖον.der: probably neuter of G2304 (θεῖος) (in its original sense of flashing);
θεῖον.as:
θεῖον, -ου, τό,
[in LXX; Ge 19:24, De 29:23 (22), Jb 18:15, Ps 10(11):7, Is 30:3334:9, Ez 38:22 (גׇּפְרִית), III Mac 2:5*;]
brimstone: Lk 17:29(LXX), Re 9:17, 1814:1019:2020:1021:8.†

θρόμβος.der: perhaps from G5142 (τρέφω) (in the sense of thickening);
θρόμβος.as:
* θρόμβος, -ου, ὁ
(< τρέφω, in primary sense to thicken),
a lump, a clot of blood (DCG, ii, 685b): αἵματος, Lk 22:44 (WH, R, mg. omit the passage, v. WH, App., 64 ff.).†

θεωρία.as:
θεωρία, -ας, ἡ
(v.s. θεωρέω), [in LXX: Da LXX 5:7, II Mac 5:2615:12, III Mac 5:24*;]
1.a viewing.
2. = θεώρημα, a spectacle, sight: Lk 23:48 (both senses in cl.).†

θρέμμα.long: (lit: a nursling, hence probably) plur: cattle.
θρέμμα.as:
* θρέμμα, -τος, τό
(τρέφω);
1.a nurseling, esp. of animals (Eur., Plat., al.).
2.cattle: Jo 4:12.†

θεοσεβής.as:
θεοσεβής, -ές
(< θεός, σέβομαι), [in LXX for אֱלֹהִיםיְרֵא, Ex 18:21, al.;]
God-fearing, godly: Jo 9:31.†
SYN.: εὐσεβής (q.v.), θρῆσκος.

θήκη.long: a repository, receptacle; a case, sheath, scabbard.
θήκη.as:
θήκη, -ης, ἡ
(< τίθημι), [in LXX: Ex 25:26(27) (בַּיִת), Is 6:13 (מַצֶּבֶת) Is 3:26*;]
a receptacle, chest, case: of the sheath of a sword, Jo 18:11.†

Θευδᾶς.long: Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C., otherwise unknown.
Θευδᾶς.as:
Θευδᾶς
(perh. contr. from Θεόδωρος, but v. MM, Exp., xv), -ᾶ, ὁ,
Theudas: Ac 5:36.†

θεομάχος.as:
**† θεομάχος, -ον,
[in Sm.: Jb 26:5, Pr 9:1821:16*;]
fighting against God: Ac 5:39.†

Θάλασσα.long: (a) the sea, in contrast to the land, (b) a particular sea or lake, e.g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.
Θάλασσα.as:
θάλασσα, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָם;]
the sea: Mt 23:15, Mk 11:23, Lk 21:25, Ro 9:27, He 11:12, Ja 1:6, Ju 13, Re 7:1, al.; τὸ πέλαγος τῆς θ. (v. Tr., ut infr.), Mt 18:6; ὁ οὐρανὸς κ. ἡ γῆ κ. ἡ θ., of the whole world, Ac 4:24, al. (Hg 2:7); θ. ὑαλίνη, Re 4:615:2; of the Mediterranean, Ac 10:6, 3217:14; of the Red Sea, ἐρυθρὰ θ., Ac 7:36, I Co 10:1, 2, He 11:29; of an inland lake (as Heb. יָם), θ. τ. Γαλιλαίας, Mt 4:1815:29, Mk 1:167:31; τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jo 21:1; τ. Γ. τ. T., Jo 6:1; of the same, simply ἡ θ., Mt 4:15, Mk 2:13, al.
SYN.: πέλαγος, the vast expanse of open water"; θ., "the sea as contrasted with the land" (Tr., Syn., xiii).

θυμομαχέω.long: (lit: I fight desperately, hence) I am furiously angry with.
θυμομαχέω.sd: to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated
θυμομαχέω.der: from a presumed compound of G2372 (θυμός) and G3164 (μάχομαι);
θυμομαχέω.as:
*† θυμομαχέω, -ῶ
(θυμός, μάχομαι),
to fight desperately, have a hot quarrel: c. dat. pers., Ac 12:20.†

Θυάτειρα.long: Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia, in the Roman province Asia.
Θυάτειρα.sd: Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor
Θυάτειρα.as:
Θυάτειρα, -ων, τά
(-ας, ἡ, Re 1:11 L; cf. WH, App., 156),
Thyatira, a city of Lydia: Ac 16:14, Re 1:112:18, 24.†

θεμέλιον.long: (properly, an adj: belonging to the foundation), a foundation stone.
θεμέλιον.sd: something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively)
θεμέλιον.as:
θεμέλιος, -ον
(< τίθημι), [in LXX for אַרְמוֹן, מוֹסָד, etc.;]
of or for a foundation; as subst., ὁ θ. (sc. λίθος), a foundation stone, foundation: Lk 6:48, 4914:29 (but v. Deiss., BS, 123); pl., οἰ θ. (cl.), He 11:10, Re 21:14, 19; neut., τὸ θ. (Arist., Phys., vi, 6, 10, LXX and later writers), Ac 16:26; metaph., Ro 15:20, I Co 3:10-12, Eph 2:20, I Ti 6:19, II Ti 2:19, He 6:1.†

Θεσσαλονίκη.long: Thessalonica (modern Saloniki), an important city of the Roman province Macedonia.
Θεσσαλονίκη.sd: Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor
Θεσσαλονίκη.as:
θεσσαλονίκη, -ης, ἡ,
Thessalonica, a city of Macedonia: Ac 17:1, 11, 13, Phl 4:16, II Ti 4:10.†

θεῖος.as:
θεῖος, -εία, -εῖον
(< θεός), [in LXX: Ex 31:335:31, Jb 27:333:4, Pr 2:17 (אֵל, אֱלוֹהַּ, אֱלֹהִים), Si 6:35, II Ma3, III Mac1, IV Mac25*;]
divine: δύναμις, II Pe 1:3; φύσις (for parallel in π., v. MM, Exp., xv), II Pe 1:4; τὸ θ., the Deity (so in cl.; of God, in Philo and FlJ), Ac 17:29.†

θεά.as:
* θεά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(fem. of θεός, q.v.),
a goddess: Ac 19:27.†

θέατρον.long: (a) a theatre, a semi-circular stone building, generally open to the sky, (b) a spectacle, show.
θέατρον.sd: a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively)
θέατρον.as:
* θέατρον, -ον, τό
(< θεάομαι),
1.a theatre (used also as a place of assembly): Ac 19:29, 31.
2. Collective for οἱ θεαταί, the spectators.
3. = θέα, θέαμα, a spectacle, show: metaph., I Co 4:9.†

Θεσσαλονικεύς.sd: a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice
Θεσσαλονικεύς.as:
θεσσαλονικεύς, -έως, ὁ,
a Thessalonian: Ac 20:427:2, I Th 1:1, II Th 1:1.†

θυρίς.as:
θυρίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(dim. of θύρα), [in LXX chiefly for חַלּוֹן;]
a window: Ac 20:9, II Co 11:33.†

θρησκεία.long: (underlying sense: reverence or worship of the gods), worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion.
θρησκεία.as:
**† θρησκεία (-κία, T), -ας, ἡ
(< θρῆσκος), [in LXX: Wi 14:18, 27, Si 22:5 A, IV Mac 5:6, 13*;]
religion in its external aspect (MM, Exp., xv), worship: Ac 26:5, Ja 1:26, 27; θ. τῶν ἀγγέλων, Col 2:18.†
SYN.: v.s. θρῆσκος.

θέρμη.as:
θέρμη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX: Jb 6:17, Ps 18(19):6, Ec 4:11 (חמם and derivatives), Si 38:28*;]
heat: Ac 28:3.†

θειότης.as:
**† θειότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< θεῖος) [in LXX: Wi 18:9*;]
divine nature, divinity: Ro 1:20 (for ex. from π., v. MM, Exp., xv).†
SYN.: θεότης, deity, godhead, divine personality. θει. = divine nature and properties, a summary term for the attributes of deity, differing from θεότης as quality or attribute from essence.

θεοστυγής.der: from G2316 (θεός) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός);
θεοστυγής.as:
* θεοστυγής, -ές
(< θεός, στυγέω),
1. passive, as freq. in cl., hateful to God: Ro 1:30 (R, txt., cf. Lit., Notes, 256).
2. Active, hating God: Ro 1:30 (R, mg., cf. ICC, in l.).†

θνητός.as:
θνητός, -ή, -όν
(< θνήσκω), [in LXX: Pr 3:1320:24 (אָדָם), Jb 30:23 (חַי), Is 51:12 (מוּת), Wi 9:1415:17, II Mac 9:12, III Mac 3:29*;]
subject to death, mortal: Ro 6:128:11, I Co 15:53, 54, II Co 4:115:4.†

θήρα.long: hunting, entrapping; prey, game; a net, means of capture.
θήρα.as:
θήρα, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX for צַיִד, טֶרֶף, רֶשֶׁת, and cogn. forms;]
1.a hunting, chase (Hdt., Xen., al.).
2.prey, game (cl.).
3. As in Ps 34(35:8) = רֶשֶׁת, a net: Ro 11:9 (but v. Thayer, s.v.).†

θηριομαχέω.long: I fight with wild beasts (i.e. wild beasts in human form); met: I am exposed to fierce hostility.
θηριομαχέω.sd: to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men)
θηριομαχέω.der: from a compound of G2342 (θηρίον) and G3164 (μάχομαι);
θηριομαχέω.as:
*† θηριομαχέω, -ῶ
(< θηρίον, μάχομαι),
to fight with wild beasts (Diod., al.): I Co 15:32.†

θριαμβεύω.g: I lead around, make a spectacle of
θριαμβεύω.long: (properly: I lead one as my prisoner in a triumphal procession, hence) I lead around, make a show (spectacle) of, cause to triumph.
θριαμβεύω.sd: and a derivative of G680 (ἅπτομαι) (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory
θριαμβεύω.der: from a prolonged compound of the base of G2360 (θροέω);
θριαμβεύω.as:
*† θριαμβεύω
(< θρίαμβος, 1. a festal hymn to Bacchus. 2. The Roman triumphus),
1.to triumph (and rarely, c. acc., to triumph over; so perh. Col 2:15, but v. infr.).
2.to lead in triumph: c. acc. pers., II Co 2:14; hence, generally, to make a spectacle or show of: Col 2:15 (but v. supr.; cf. MM, Exp., xv; and esp. Field, Notes, 181).†

θαρρέω.g: I am courageous, of good cheer
θαρρέω.long: I am courageous, confident, of good cheer.
θαρρέω.kj: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident
θαρρέω.as:
θαρρέω, -ῶ
(later form of θαρσέω), [in LXX: Pr 1:21, Ba 4:21, 27, Da LXX 6:16 (17), IV Mac 13:1117:4*;]
to be of good cheer or courage, to be confident: II Co 5:6, 8, He 13:6; τ. πεποιθήσει, II Co 10:2; seq. εἰς, II Co 10:1; ἐν, II Co 7:16.†
SYN.: τολμάω. "θ. has reference more to the character, τ. to its manifestation" (Thayer, s.v. τολμάω).

θαῦμα.long: (a) concr: a marvel, wonder, (b) abstr: wonder, amazement.
θαῦμα.sd: wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract)
θαῦμα.der: apparently from a form of G2300 (θεάομαι);
θαῦμα.as:
θαῦμα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX: Jb 17:818:2020:821:5 (שַׂעַר, etc.)*;]
1.a wonder: II Co 11:14.
2.wonder: Re 17:6.†

θάλπω.long: (properly: I warm, then) I cherish, nourish, foster, comfort.
θάλπω.as:
θάλπω,
[in LXX for סכן, etc.;]
to heat, warm; metaph.,
(a)to inflame (Trag.);
(b)to foster, cherish: Eph 5:29, I Th 2:7.†

θώραξ.sd: the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet
θώραξ.as:
θώραξ, -ακσς, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁרְיוֹן and cogn. forms;]
a breastplate: Re 9:9, 17; θ. τ. δικαιοσύνης, Eph 6:14 (cf. Is 59:17, Wi 5:18(19)); θ. πίστεως, I Th 5:8.†

θυρεός.as:
θυρεός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< θύρα), [in LXX for מָגֵן, צִנָּה;]
1. in Hom., a door-stone.
2. In late Gk. (Polyb., Plut.), the scutum, a large oblong shield: θ. τ. πίστεως, Eph 6:16 (cf. Wi 5:20, where ὁσιότης is likened to the ἀσπίς, the clypeus or small round shield of the light-armed soldier).†

θιγγάνω.sd: to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure
θιγγάνω.der: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (to finger);
θιγγάνω.as:
θιγγάνω,
[in LXX for נגע, Ex 19:12*;]
1.to touch, handle: Col 2:21, He 12:20(LXX).
2.to injure (like Heb. נגע, and as in Eur., Iph. Aul., 1351): c. gen., He 11:28.†
SYN.: v.s. ἅπτω.

θεοδίδακτος.as:
*† θεο-δίδακτος, -ον,
taught of God (cf. διδακτοὶ θεοῦ, Jo 6:45): I Th 4:9.†

θεοσέβεια.long: reverence for God, fear of God, godliness, piety.
θεοσέβεια.as:
θεοσέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(< θεοσεβής), [in LXX: Ge 20:11 (אֱלֹהִיםיִרְאַה), Jb 28:28 (אֲדֹנָי id.), Si 1:24, Ba 5:4, IV Mac 7:6, 22, אIV Mac 15:28אIV Mac 17:15*;]
fear of God, godliness: I Ti 2:10.†

θεόπνευστος.long: God-breathed, inspired by God, due to the inspiration of God.
θεόπνευστος.der: from G2316 (θεός) and a presumed derivative of G4154 (πνέω);
θεόπνευστος.as:
*† θεόπνευστος, -ον
(< θεός, πνέω),
inspired by God: II Ti 3:16.†

θέλησις.as:
† θέλησις, -εως, ἡ
(θέλω), [in LXX: II Ch 15:15, Pr 8:35 (רָצוֹן), Ez 18:23 (חֵפֶץ), Da LXX 11:45 (צְבִי), To 12:18, Wi 16:25, II Mac 12:16, III Mac 2:26*;]
in colloq. and MGr. = τὸ θέλειν, will: He 2:4.†

θεράπων.der: apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of G2330 (θέρος);
θεράπων.as:
θεράπων, -οντος, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for עֶבֶד;]
an attendant, servant: He 3:5(LXX).†
SYN.: v.s. διάκονος.

θυμιατήριον.long: (ordinarily: censer, but) either the altar of incense, or the shovel, on which the high-priest poured the coals, when he entered the Holy of Holies on the Day of Atonement.
θυμιατήριον.sd: a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple)
θυμιατήριον.as:
θυμιατήριον, -ου, τό
(< θυμιάω), [in LXX: II Ch 26:19, Ez 8:11 (מִקְטֶרֶת), IV Mac 7:11*;]
1. as in cl. (Hdt., iv, 162; Thuc., vi, 46) and LXX, a censer: He 9:4 (but v. infr., and cf. Westc., in l.).
2. As in Philo., rer. div., § 46, FlJ, Ant., iv, 2, 4, al., the altar of incense: He 9:4 (but v. supr. and cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

θεατρίζω.g: I make a public show of
θεατρίζω.long: I make a public show of, expose to public shame.
θεατρίζω.as:
*† θεατρίζω
(< θέατρον),
to make a spectacle of, expose to contempt (eccl.; ἐκθ-, Polyb.): pass., He 10:33.†

θύελλα.der: from G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of blowing) a storm
θύελλα.as:
θύελλα, -ης, ἡ
(< θύω), [in LXX De 4:115:22 (19) (עֲרָפֶל), Ex 10:22*;] (poët. in cl.),
a hurricane, cyclone, whirlwind: He 12:18.†
SYN.: λαῖλαψ (q.v.).

θρησκός.long: (refers probably to a careful observance of religious restrictions), religious (probably in a limited sense), devout.
θρησκός.sd: ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious
θρησκός.der: probably from the base of G2360 (θροέω);
θρησκός.as:
* θρῆσκος
(-κός, WH), -ου, ὁ
religious, careful of the outward forms of divine service (see previous word): Ja 1:26.†
SYN.: εὐσεβής, θεοσεβής, δεισιδαίμων (v. Tr., Syn., § xlviii).

θανατηφόρος.der: from (the feminine form of) G2288 (θάνατος) and G5342 (φέρω);
θανατηφόρος.as:
θανατη-φόρος, -ον
(< θάνατος, φέρω), [in LXX: Nu 18:22 (מוּת), Jb 33:23, IV Mac 8:18, 2615:26*;]
deadly, death-bringing: Ja 3:8.†

θύϊνος.sd: denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood
θύϊνος.der: from a derivative of G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of blowing;
θύϊνος.as:
**† θύινος (usually θύϊνος, as Rec.), -η, -ον
(< θυία, θύα, an African aromatic tree, with ornamentally veined wood of varying colour, = Lat. citrinus), [in Sm.: III Ki 10:11 (אַלְמֻגִּים)*;]
thyine: ξύλον, Re 18:12 (Diosc.).†
